# Two-worker integration and resumable finite batches

Owner authorization: November 3, 2026 — proceed with the recommended two-worker integration, input reuse and safely resumable larger batches; automatically return to the working configuration if unsuccessful.

One controller and one production slot remain exclusive. `maxConcurrency: 1` continues to bound campaign/slot ownership; `resumableBatch.workers: 2` explicitly describes the two child processes inside that slot. Every pair passes combined worst-case source, request, attempt, summed child-seconds, output, physical-cache and closure-deadline admission before either child starts. No source retry, identity expansion, budget expansion or renderer-quality change is introduced.

Each child has an independent SQLite database and working directory. Already verified immutable COG blocks are hard-linked locally. Between pairs, source identities must agree, new range hashes are checked, and both append-only transfer histories are merged without duplicating their common prefix. The next pair reuses the combined inputs. Service exports and overview rendering stay outside this first paired source implementation. Existing raw Cloud cache objects remain untouched; new working ranges remain transient under the existing policy.

The producer closes an exact ordered attempted prefix and untouched tail after every submitted child has exited. Independent recovery reads every immutable reservation and checks parent/child resource conservation, accepted output receipts, full retained allowances for quarantined attempts, typed source-gap evidence, merged source ledgers and the unchanged pixel/seam/package QA. Only a verified closure may reach the planner. The trusted publisher separately checks accepted history, attempt counters, quarantines and the next policy.

Rollout is bounded: two successful measured 12-job paired waves, then two successful measured 24-job waves, then continued 24-job waves. No automatic growth beyond 24 is implemented. The gate measures actual GitHub dispatch-to-independent-recovery tile throughput, including input bootstrap and independent QA; it does not extrapolate the earlier rendering-only microbenchmark. Publication time is outside that timing interval and must be included separately in any reported whole-cycle throughput. A substantial regression, two consecutive sub-baseline waves, a failed child/checkpoint, or an incomplete eligible batch causes the next fresh allocation to use the preserved serial 12-job function. The controller disables re-enrollment after fallback. Accepted receipts, source identities, budgets and every consumed attempt are carried forward; historical rollback ledgers are never restored.

An interrupted or unverifiable closure cannot safely prove which source attempts remain unused. It stays fail-closed rather than replaying ambiguous work. This is distinct from a cleanly closed failed pilot, which automatically continues in serial mode.

Validation: focused adversarial tests exercise actual separate subprocesses with explicitly synthetic output, isolated SQLite writers and range reuse, resource exits, consecutive source gaps, checkpoint response loss, duplicate claims, altered closure records and automatic performance fallback. Seven synthetic migration/prepare/trusted-publication roundtrips exercise 12 → 24 → active → partial closure → serial fallback and a later serial successor. These tests do not establish live raster coverage. Exact-head broader regression and live rollout evidence are recorded separately after completion.
